title: Lelouch vs Schneizel Analysed like Chess | Code Geass

source_quality.note: Original is 1280x720. Marked technical preview only; replace and realign for final HD.

opening.speaker: white
opening.label: Lelouch
opening.evidence: At 0.52-5.42s Lelouch on the screen asks about using Damocles to dominate the world; source frame at 1s reviewed.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Schneizel calls human nature a matter of opinion. His peace plan needs people to stop changing. That is a risky assumption to build your endgame on.

annotations.speaker: black
annotations.comment: Schneizel is ready to die. But he has decided what winning means for Lelouch without checking. That assumption is about to become expensive.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Lelouch orders Schneizel to serve Zero. Killing him would waste a useful piece. Taking control wins the position and keeps the piece.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Schneizel was arguing with a recording. Lelouch predicted his answers and used the debate to conceal his approach. The conversation was the decoy.

annotations.speaker: white
annotations.comment: Schneizel shoots Diethard to protect Lelouch. The enemy piece has changed sides. Diethard notices the new team arrangement one move too late.
